The glyf table's iov entries point directly into the input font data buffer, not into the output stream.

note: The glyf table serializes by writing each iov entry to the output stream. The iov entries point to the original input data buffer.
OTSStream::Write is called with data pointing to the input font data (from glyf's iov entries) and length being the glyph data size.

code: if (chksum) { const uint8_t *p = static_cast<const uint8_t*>(data); for (size_t i = 0; i < length; ++i) { chksum += p[i]; } }
note: The checksum is computed over the input data before calling WriteRaw. This reads from the input buffer which is still valid at this point.
WriteRaw is called with the data pointer. If the output stream needs to grow, the old buffer will be freed while data may still point into it.
Checks if the current write would exceed the buffer capacity. If so, the buffer needs to grow.

note: A new larger buffer is allocated and the old contents are copied to it.
The old buffer is freed. If the data parameter points into this old buffer (which happens when the input data is the same as the stream's buffer), this creates a use-after-free.
The recursive call reads from the freed old buffer, causing a heap-use-after-free when the data pointer references the deallocated memory.
The memcpy reads from the freed memory region, triggering the heap-use-after-free detected by ASan.
